summary:
NASA has sent many machines to the Moon and Mars to explore their surfaces and help scientists understand space. Although some missions have ended, their equipment remains behind as a reminder of human discovery.

1. The Moon – Equipment Left Behind
- Apollo Lunar Module descent stages were left on the Moon after astronauts returned to Earth.
- Lunar Roving Vehicles helped astronauts travel across the lunar surface.
- Scientific instruments and Surveyor landers helped scientists study the Moon.
2. Mars – Robots That Never Came Home
- Sojourner, Spirit and Opportunity explored Mars and sent valuable information back to Earth.
- Viking, Phoenix and InSight studied the Martian surface and environment.
- Ingenuity became the first aircraft to achieve powered flight on another planet.
3. Beyond the Moon and Mars
- Dawn explored the asteroids Vesta and Ceres.
- NEAR Shoemaker landed on the asteroid Eros.
- Pioneer 10 and 11 travelled far beyond the outer planets.
- Kepler discovered thousands of planets beyond our solar system.
Conclusion

Even though many of these machines can no longer operate, their discoveries continue to help scientists understand the universe. They remind us that a mission may end, but its contribution to science is never forgotten.

Abandoned but Not Forgotten: NASA's Forgotten Machines of the Moon and Mars

1. Introduction

Space exploration has allowed humans to discover more about the Moon and Mars. NASA has sent astronauts, robots, landers and scientific equipment to explore these places. However, when some missions ended, the machines were left behind because they could not return to Earth.

These machines may no longer be working, but they played an important role in scientific discoveries. This project explores some of NASA's equipment left on the Moon and Mars and explains why these machines are important to space exploration.

2. Project Objectives

  • To learn about NASA's space exploration missions.
  • To identify equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars.
  • To understand the purpose of lunar landers, rovers and helicopters.
  • To explain how these machines helped scientists.
  • To appreciate the importance of technology and scientific exploration.

3. Project Scope

This project focuses on three main topics:

Topic 1: Equipment Left on the Moon

  • Apollo Lunar Module descent stages
  • Lunar Roving Vehicles
  • Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP)
  • Surveyor robotic landers

Topic 2: Robots Left on Mars

  • Sojourner rover
  • Spirit and Opportunity rovers
  • Viking landers
  • Phoenix and InSight landers

Topic 3: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter

  • First aircraft to achieve powered, controlled flight on another planet.
  • Completed 72 flights on Mars.
  • Its mission ended in 2024 after rotor damage.

4. Three-Slide Presentation Plan

Slide 1: The Moon – A Legacy Left Behind

Explain how Apollo astronauts left equipment on the Moon after completing their missions. Include pictures of the Apollo Lunar Module and Lunar Roving Vehicle.

Slide 2: Mars – Robots That Never Came Home

Introduce Sojourner, Spirit and Opportunity. Explain how these rovers explored the Martian surface, studied rocks and helped scientists understand the planet.

Slide 3: Ingenuity – The First Helicopter on Mars

Describe Ingenuity's historic flights, its achievements and how it became a stationary artifact after its mission ended.

5. Project Method

The project will be completed through the following steps:

  1. Research information about NASA's Moon and Mars missions.
  2. Select important examples of equipment left behind.
  3. Collect suitable space images and illustrations.
  4. Prepare three presentation slides in a 16:9 format.
  5. Write a short English explanation for each slide.
  6. Present the information in a clear and interesting way.

6. Expected Outcomes

After completing this project, viewers should:

  • Recognise important NASA equipment left on the Moon and Mars.
  • Understand the purpose of different space machines.
  • Learn about the achievements of NASA's robotic missions.
  • Understand that equipment can remain important even after a mission ends.

7. Conclusion

NASA's abandoned machines are more than forgotten equipment. They represent human curiosity, courage, technology and scientific achievement. Although many of these machines have stopped working, the information they collected continues to help scientists learn about space.

Project Message: A mission may end, but its discoveries are never forgotten.
